question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'

She's considered one/ of a best young/ directors in Hollywood.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. of a best young

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is the article "a" before the superlative "best".

◦ Rule: a superlative degree is always preceded by the definite article "the", never by "a/an" — the best, the tallest, the most beautiful.

◦ Moreover, the structure "one of the + superlative + plural noun" is fixed: one of the best young directors.

◦ Corrected sentence: She's considered one of the best young directors in Hollywood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment "She's considered one" is correct — the contraction She's (She is) with the passive "is considered" is fine.

• Segment "directors in Hollywood." is correct — the plural noun is right after "one of the best".

NOTE

• Golden rule: one of the + superlative + plural noun + singular verb — One of the tallest buildings in the world is in Dubai.

• "The" is used with superlatives, ordinals (the first, the second), unique things (the sun, the moon) and with adjectives used as nouns (the rich, the poor).

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

Paul Bunyan is considered a legend.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. tradition.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "legend" is an old, popular story handed down from the past, which may or may not be true; it also means a person who is famous and admired for a long time. (किंवदंती)

◦ Among the options, "tradition" is the closest, since a tradition is also a belief, story or custom passed down from generation to generation.

◦ Paul Bunyan is a giant lumberjack of American folklore, precisely the kind of figure who exists as a legend/tradition handed down over time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "spinster" = an unmarried woman, usually one beyond the usual age of marriage.

• Option 2 "stoic" = a person who endures pain or hardship without showing feelings or complaining.

• Option 3 "volunteer" = a person who offers to do something without being forced or paid.

NOTE

• Synonyms of legend: myth, folklore, folk tale, tradition, saga, fable.

• Distinguish: a myth explains natural or religious phenomena; a legend is loosely based on historical fact; a fable teaches a moral, usually through animals.

• "Legend" also means the explanatory key of a map or diagram.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I am going to take you for a ______ up there.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ride.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression is "take somebody for a ride", meaning to take a person on a journey in a vehicle (literally), and the phrase "up there" points to a place being travelled to.

◦ The blank follows the article "a", so a noun is required, and "ride" is the only noun among the options that fits.

◦ Correct: I am going to take you for a ride up there.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "rite" = a religious or solemn ceremony (funeral rites, rites of passage).

• Option 2 "write" is a verb and cannot follow the article 'a'.

• Option 4 "right" means correct, a moral entitlement, or the opposite of left — none of which suits "take you for a ______".

NOTE

• Homophones to remember: rite / write / right / wright (a maker, as in playwright).

• Note the idiomatic second meaning: "take somebody for a ride" can also mean to cheat or deceive someone — The salesman took him for a ride.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A residence for monks or priests
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Monastery.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Monastery" is a building or complex in which monks live as a religious community. (मठ / विहार)

◦ The word comes from the Greek monos = alone, the same root as monk and monastic.

◦ Example: The Buddhist monastery at Tawang is one of the largest in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Nursery" = a place where young children are cared for, or where young plants are grown.

• Option 2 "Convent" = a residence for nuns — the female counterpart, so it is the trap option here since the question specifies monks or priests.

• Option 4 "Tomb" = a grave or burial structure.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions of place: hermitage (a hermit's dwelling), presbytery/rectory (a priest's house), abbey (a monastery headed by an abbot), seminary (a training college for priests), vihara (a Buddhist monastery).

• The Buddhist monastery is called a Vihara and the prayer hall a Chaitya.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The accountant of the sugar mill have been deprived of his briefcase.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. has been deprived.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "The accountant" — a singular noun. The phrase "of the sugar mill" is a prepositional phrase and does not affect the number of the subject.

◦ A singular subject takes "has", so the correct present perfect passive form is "has been deprived".

◦ The possessive "his" later in the sentence also confirms that the subject is singular.

◦ Corrected sentence: The accountant of the sugar mill has been deprived of his briefcase.

◦ Note the collocation: "deprive somebody of something".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "was being deprived" is past continuous passive and does not fit the completed sense of the sentence.

• Option 3 "No improvement" is wrong because "have" does not agree with the singular subject.

• Option 4 "is deprive" is ungrammatical — the base form cannot follow 'is'; it would need the participle deprived.

NOTE

• Rule: the verb agrees with the head noun, not with a noun inside an intervening phrase — The quality of the mangoes was poor.

• Present perfect passive = has/have been + V3; past perfect passive = had been + V3.

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Awful
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Wonderful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Awful" means very bad, unpleasant or terrible. (भयानक / बहुत बुरा)

◦ Its direct antonym is "Wonderful" — extremely good, delightful or admirable. (अद्भुत)

◦ Example: The weather was awful yesterday, but today it is wonderful.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Pitiful" = arousing pity; very inadequate — negative, like 'awful'.

• Option 2 "Dreadful" = causing great fear or suffering; very bad — a close synonym of awful, planted as a trap.

• Option 3 "Grim" = stern, gloomy or depressing — again negative.

NOTE

• Synonyms of awful: dreadful, terrible, horrible, appalling, atrocious, ghastly.

• Antonyms of awful: wonderful, marvellous, delightful, excellent, superb, splendid.

• Note the shift in meaning over time: awful originally meant "full of awe / awe-inspiring", a sense preserved in awesome.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Many female mammals, including rabbits and cats, ovulate only when they mate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No error

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Many female mammals, including rabbits and cats, ovulate only when they mate." is grammatically correct in every respect.

◦ "Many female mammals" is a plural subject, correctly matched with the plural verb "ovulate".

◦ The phrase "including rabbits and cats" is a parenthetical (non-defining) element, correctly enclosed within a pair of commas; it does not affect the subject–verb agreement.

◦ "only when they mate" is a properly formed time clause, and the pronoun "they" agrees with the plural subject.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Placement rule: the adverb "only" should stand as close as possible to the word it limits — here it correctly limits the time clause "when they mate".

• Words such as including, along with, as well as, together with, in addition to, besides never change the number of the subject: The teacher, along with the students, was present.

NOTE

• A non-defining phrase is set off by commas and merely adds information; a defining phrase takes no commas and identifies the noun.

• In error-spotting questions, remember that "No error" is a genuine and fairly frequent answer in SSC papers — do not manufacture a fault.

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: Your emergency contacts couldn't be reached.
option_2: Your emergency contatcs couldn't be reached.
option_3: Your emergancy contacts couldn't be reached.
option_4: Your emergency contacts coldn't be reaced.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Your emergency contacts couldn't be reached.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Option 1 every word is spelt correctly — "emergency", "contacts", "couldn't" and "reached".

◦ Emergency = e-m-e-r-g-e-n-c-y, ending in -ency, not -ancy.

◦ Contacts = c-o-n-t-a-c-t-s.

◦ Couldn't = the contraction of could not, with the apostrophe replacing the missing o.

◦ Reached = r-e-a-c-h-e-d.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 — "contatcs" has its letters transposed; the correct spelling is "contacts".

• Option 3 — "emergancy" is wrong; the correct spelling is "emergency".

• Option 4 — two errors: "coldn't" should be "couldn't" and "reaced" should be "reached".

NOTE

• Nouns ending in -ency: emergency, efficiency, frequency, urgency, tendency, consistency.

• Nouns ending in -ancy: vacancy, hesitancy, occupancy, relevancy — the ending usually follows the adjective form (efficient → efficiency; vacant → vacancy).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

My history assignment is due on Wednesday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined part "is due on" is completely correct and needs no change.

◦ The subject "My history assignment" is singular, so the singular verb "is" is right.

◦ "Due" means expected to be handed in or to happen at a particular time, and the correct preposition before a day of the week is "on" — on Wednesday, on Monday, on 15 August.

◦ Correct sentence as printed: My history assignment is due on Wednesday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "are due at" has a plural verb for a singular subject and the wrong preposition.

• Option 3 "were due on" is plural and past, both wrong here.

• Option 4 "is dues in" wrongly makes 'due' a plural noun and uses the wrong preposition.

NOTE

• Prepositions of time: on + days and dates (on Sunday, on 5 June); in + months, years, seasons, parts of the day (in May, in 2023, in the morning); at + clock time and festivals (at 6 o'clock, at noon, at Diwali).

• Useful expressions with due: due to (because of), in due course (at the proper time), due date, overdue.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To see the light
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Suddenly realize or understand something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to see the light" means to suddenly understand or realise something that was not clear before; it also means to be convinced of a truth after a period of doubt. (अचानक समझ में आना)

◦ Example: After hours of explanation, he finally saw the light and admitted his mistake.

◦ A related phrase, "see the light of day", means to be made public or to come into existence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To gain conscious" would correspond to regain consciousness, which is expressed by come round / come to.

• Option 2 "To misunderstand the situation" is the opposite of the idiom's meaning — it corresponds to get hold of the wrong end of the stick.

• Option 3 "To be optimistic" is expressed by look on the bright side.

NOTE

• Other 'understanding' idioms: the penny dropped (suddenly understood), ring a bell (sound familiar), get the picture, it dawned on me.

• Other 'light' idioms: in the light of (considering), light at the end of the tunnel (hope after difficulty), bring to light (reveal), many moons ago (long ago).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The sedative effect of the drugs impairs people's ability to pay attention and ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. concentrate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is joined by "and" to the phrase "pay attention", so the missing verb must belong to the same field of meaning — mental focus.

◦ "Concentrate" means to give all one's attention to something, and it pairs naturally with 'pay attention'.

◦ Correct: The sedative effect of the drugs impairs people's ability to pay attention and concentrate.

◦ A "sedative" is a drug that makes a person calm or sleepy, so it would naturally reduce alertness and focus.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "segregate" = to separate or set apart from others.

• Option 3 "reverberate" = to echo repeatedly; to resound.

• Option 4 "dilate" = to become wider or larger (the pupils dilate in dim light).

NOTE

• Parallelism rule: words joined by and must be of the same grammatical form and belong to the same sense-group — the ability to pay attention and (to) concentrate.

• "Impair" in the sentence means to weaken or damage the quality or function of something; word family: impair, impairment, impaired.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

One-to-one interaction with parents is know to be important.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. with parents is know

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is the use of the base form "know" where the past participle "known" is required.

◦ The sentence is in the passive voice, whose structure is be + past participle (V3), so it must read "is known".

◦ Verb forms: know – knew – known.

◦ Corrected sentence: One-to-one interaction with parents is known to be important.

◦ The singular verb "is" is correct, since the subject "One-to-one interaction" is singular.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment "One-to-one interaction" is correct — the compound adjective is properly hyphenated before the noun.

• Segment "to be important." is correct — the structure "is known to be + adjective" is standard English.

NOTE

• Common passive patterns with reporting verbs: is known/said/believed/thought/considered/reported + to be.

• Hyphenate compound adjectives before a noun: a well-known writer, a five-year plan, a state-of-the-art facility — but not after the noun: The writer is well known.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

(Hardly did the ink dried on my weekly column, when) one of my readers called me.
option_1: Hardly had the ink dry on last week's column, when
option_3: Hardly did the ink dried on last week's column, when
option_4: Hardly had the ink dried on last week's column, when
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Hardly had the ink dried on last week's column, when

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the fixed structure "Hardly ... when", which describes one action happening immediately before another.

◦ Rule: when a sentence begins with a negative adverb such as hardly, scarcely, barely, seldom, rarely, never, no sooner, the word order is inverted and the past perfect is used in the first clause:

◦ Hardly + had + subject + V3 ... when + simple past.

◦ So the correct form is "Hardly had the ink dried ... when one of my readers called me."

◦ Corrected sentence: Hardly had the ink dried on last week's column, when one of my readers called me.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 uses the base form "dry" instead of the past participle dried.

• Options 2 and 3 keep "did ... dried" — a double error, since the auxiliary did must be followed by the base form, and in any case the structure requires had.

NOTE

• Parallel structures to memorise: Hardly/Scarcely ... when; No sooner ... than; Barely ... when.

◦ No sooner had he arrived than it started raining.

• Other inversions: Seldom does he complain; Never have I seen such a sight.

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Inquisitive
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Curious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inquisitive" means eager to know or learn something; asking a lot of questions (sometimes with the sense of prying). (जिज्ञासु)

◦ "Curious" carries exactly this sense of eagerness to know, and is the closest synonym.

◦ Example: The inquisitive (curious) child kept asking why the sky was blue.

◦ Word family: inquire/enquire (verb), inquiry (noun), inquisitive (adjective), inquisition (a searching investigation).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Agile" = able to move quickly and easily; nimble, also used of a quick mind.

• Option 2 "Aloof" = distant and not friendly; keeping apart from others — almost the opposite of an inquisitive nature.

• Option 3 "Callous" = unfeeling and insensitive to the suffering of others.

NOTE

• Synonyms of inquisitive: curious, questioning, probing, inquiring, nosy, prying.

• Antonyms of inquisitive: indifferent, uninterested, apathetic, unconcerned.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

______ months later, Steve returned to New York to look for a job.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A few.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Months" is a plural countable noun, so the determiner must be few / a few, not little / a little.

◦ The sentence simply states that some months passed before Steve returned, which is a positive statement — and "a few" means some, a small number (positive sense).

◦ "Few" without the article means hardly any / almost none (negative sense) and would wrongly suggest that scarcely any months passed.

◦ Correct: A few months later, Steve returned to New York to look for a job.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "The few" means the small number that exists, and needs a defining context (the few friends he had), which is absent here.

• Option 4 "A little" is used only with uncountable nouns (a little water, a little time), never with 'months'.

NOTE

• Quick guide: few = hardly any (negative); a few = some (positive); the few = the small number there is. Similarly little = hardly any; a little = some; the little = the small amount there is.

• Use few/a few with countable nouns and little/a little with uncountable nouns.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

She kept pictures of her parents all ______ the house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. over.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression is "all over", meaning everywhere in or throughout a place.

◦ Correct: She kept pictures of her parents all over the house.

◦ It conveys that the pictures were placed in every part of the house.

◦ Example: There were books all over the floor.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "all about" is not the standard collocation for physical scattering in a place in modern usage.

• Option 3 "all through" is used chiefly for time — all through the night, all through the year.

• Option 4 "all out" is a different idiom meaning with maximum effort (go all out to win).

NOTE

• Useful expressions with over: all over (everywhere), over and over (repeatedly), be over (finished), get over (recover from), look over (examine), over the moon (delighted).

• "All over the world/country/place" is a very common collocation worth memorising.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

One hard to please (very selective in his habits)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Fastidious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fastidious" means very attentive to detail and hard to please; excessively particular about accuracy, cleanliness or taste. (नकचढ़ा / अति सतर्क)

◦ Example: He is so fastidious about his food that he will not eat at any restaurant.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Dexterous" = skilful with the hands; showing mental skill.

• Option 2 "Incorrigible" = impossible to correct or reform (an incorrigible liar).

• Option 3 "Sadist" = a person who derives pleasure from inflicting pain on others.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fastidious: meticulous, finicky, particular, punctilious, scrupulous, choosy.

• Antonyms of fastidious: careless, easy-going, undemanding, slovenly.

• Related one-word substitutions of temperament: misanthrope (hater of mankind), misogynist (hater of women), philanthropist (lover of mankind), egotist (self-centred person), stoic (one indifferent to pain or pleasure).

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Moking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word is wrongly spelt; the correct spelling is "Mocking" — m-o-c-k-i-n-g, with a 'ck'.

◦ Mock means to laugh at somebody in an unkind way; to ridicule; as an adjective it means not real (a mock test, a mock trial).

◦ Spelling rule: a short vowel sound before the /k/ sound is normally written -ck, as in mock, lock, rock, kick, back, duck.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Plus" is correct — meaning with the addition of, or an advantage.

• Option 2 "Dearest" is correct — the superlative of dear (dear – dearer – dearest).

• Option 3 "Worry" is correct — to be anxious; note the plural worries and the past worried (y changes to i).

NOTE

• Word family: mock (verb/adjective), mockery (noun), mocking (adjective), mockingly (adverb).

• Verbs ending in a consonant + y change y to i before adding endings: worry → worried, carry → carried, study → studied.

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

The tension is going to be crucial in determining the fate of your company.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. trivial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Crucial" means extremely important; decisive in determining an outcome. (निर्णायक / अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण)

◦ Its antonym must mean of very little importance, and "trivial" means exactly that — unimportant, insignificant, of little value. (तुच्छ / मामूली)

◦ Example: This is a crucial decision, not a trivial one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "decisive" and Option 4 "pivotal" are both synonyms of crucial — deliberately planted traps.

• Option 1 "surgical" = relating to surgery, or (figuratively) precise and targeted; it is unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of crucial: vital, critical, decisive, pivotal, essential, key.

• Antonyms of crucial: trivial, unimportant, insignificant, negligible, minor, petty.

• The word comes from Latin crux = a cross, the idea being a crossroads where a decisive choice must be made.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

From rags to riches
option_3: To toil very hard to gain something
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. From extreme poverty to wealth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "from rags to riches" describes the rise of a person from a state of extreme poverty to great wealth and success. (गरीबी से अमीरी तक)

◦ "Rags" are old torn clothes, symbolising poverty; "riches" stand for wealth.

◦ Example: His life story is a classic rags-to-riches tale — he began as a newspaper boy and now owns a media company.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "From everywhere" would be expressed by from far and wide or from all quarters.

• Option 2 "Reasonable pricing" has no connection with the idiom.

• Option 3 "To toil very hard to gain something" corresponds to sweat blood or burn the midnight oil.

NOTE

• Related wealth-and-poverty idioms: born with a silver spoon in one's mouth (born rich), make ends meet (manage on limited money), hand to mouth (living with barely enough), strike it rich (suddenly become wealthy), a self-made man.

• The opposite journey is described by the idiom from riches to rags.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Red kites were considered vermin across Britain and Ireland (1) ______ the 16th century and their numbers were rigorously (2) ______. While public perceptions have changed, gamekeepers and farmers still (3) ______ shoot, poison and trap red kites for the (4) ______ harm they cause to livestock and game. In 2020 alone, 20 red kites were confirmed to have been (5) ______ this way in the UK.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. during.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by the noun phrase "the 16th century", which is a period of time, so the preposition "during" — meaning throughout or at some point in a period — is required.

◦ Correct: Red kites were considered vermin across Britain and Ireland during the 16th century.

◦ "During + noun" is the standard structure: during the war, during the holidays, during the meeting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "while" is a conjunction and must be followed by a clause (subject + verb), not by a noun phrase.

• Option 2 "along" indicates movement or position beside a line (along the river).

• Option 4 "across" indicates movement or extent from one side to the other — it is already used earlier in the sentence ("across Britain and Ireland") and cannot serve for time.

NOTE

• Remember: during + noun (during the lesson) versus while + clause (while the lesson was going on).

• "Vermin" in the passage means wild animals or birds regarded as pests that are harmful to crops, game or livestock.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Red kites were considered vermin across Britain and Ireland (1) ______ the 16th century and their numbers were rigorously (2) ______. While public perceptions have changed, gamekeepers and farmers still (3) ______ shoot, poison and trap red kites for the (4) ______ harm they cause to livestock and game. In 2020 alone, 20 red kites were confirmed to have been (5) ______ this way in the UK.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. controlled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence says that because red kites were treated as vermin, their numbers were deliberately reduced and kept in check — the standard term for this is "controlled".

◦ The adverb "rigorously" (strictly, severely) fits naturally with 'controlled'.

◦ Correct: ... and their numbers were rigorously controlled.

◦ In wildlife management, "population control" is exactly the phrase used for such culling.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "changed" is too vague and does not convey deliberate reduction.

• Option 2 "choked" means blocked or unable to breathe, which does not collocate with 'numbers'.

• Option 4 "loosened" means made less tight, the opposite of restricting.

NOTE

• Useful collocations with control: control the population/price/situation/damage; under control; out of control; pest control.

• The red kite is a bird of prey whose population in Britain recovered dramatically through one of the world's most successful conservation reintroduction programmes.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Red kites were considered vermin across Britain and Ireland (1) ______ the 16th century and their numbers were rigorously (2) ______. While public perceptions have changed, gamekeepers and farmers still (3) ______ shoot, poison and trap red kites for the (4) ______ harm they cause to livestock and game. In 2020 alone, 20 red kites were confirmed to have been (5) ______ this way in the UK.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. illegally.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence sets up a contrast — "While public perceptions have changed, gamekeepers and farmers still ______ shoot, poison and trap red kites."

◦ Since attitudes and the law have changed and the bird is now protected, any killing of red kites today is against the law — hence "illegally".

◦ The word "still" reinforces that the practice continues even though it is now forbidden.

◦ Correct: ... gamekeepers and farmers still illegally shoot, poison and trap red kites.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "randomly" (without any pattern) misses the point of the contrast.

• Option 3 "fairly" means justly or moderately, which contradicts the disapproving tone.

• Option 4 "unknowingly" is wrong because shooting, poisoning and trapping are clearly deliberate acts.

NOTE

• Contrast signposts in cloze passages: while, whereas, although, though, even though, however, still, yet, nevertheless.

• The prefix il- means not before words beginning with l: illegal, illiterate, illogical, illegible.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Red kites were considered vermin across Britain and Ireland (1) ______ the 16th century and their numbers were rigorously (2) ______. While public perceptions have changed, gamekeepers and farmers still (3) ______ shoot, poison and trap red kites for the (4) ______ harm they cause to livestock and game. In 2020 alone, 20 red kites were confirmed to have been (5) ______ this way in the UK.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. perceived.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an adjective before "harm they cause to livestock and game", and the writer's point is that this harm is believed in rather than proved — the exact word for that is "perceived".

◦ "Perceived" means as seen or believed by people, though not necessarily true in fact.

◦ Correct: ... shoot, poison and trap red kites for the perceived harm they cause to livestock and game.

◦ This also links back to "public perceptions" mentioned in the same sentence — the same root word, a strong contextual clue.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "kicked" and Option 4 "shipped" make no sense with 'harm'.

• Option 2 "dirty" does not describe harm in this sense.

NOTE

• Word family: perceive (verb), perception (noun), perceptible (able to be noticed), perceptive (quick to notice and understand).

• In cloze passages, a repeated root word elsewhere in the paragraph (here perceptions) is one of the most reliable clues to the missing word.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Red kites were considered vermin across Britain and Ireland (1) ______ the 16th century and their numbers were rigorously (2) ______. While public perceptions have changed, gamekeepers and farmers still (3) ______ shoot, poison and trap red kites for the (4) ______ harm they cause to livestock and game. In 2020 alone, 20 red kites were confirmed to have been (5) ______ this way in the UK.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. killed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The previous sentence lists the methods used against red kites — "shoot, poison and trap" — all of which result in the death of the bird.

◦ Therefore "20 red kites were confirmed to have been killed this way in the UK" is the only logical completion.

◦ The phrase "this way" refers directly back to those illegal methods.

◦ Grammar point: the structure is the perfect passive infinitive — to have been + V3 — so the past participle killed is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "awakened" (woken up) contradicts the sense of the passage entirely.

• Option 3 "subjected" would need the preposition to (subjected to cruelty) and cannot stand alone here.

• Option 4 "rooted" means fixed firmly in place or established.

NOTE

• Passive infinitive forms: to be + V3 (present) and to have been + V3 (perfect) — He is said to have been killed in the accident.

• Related conservation vocabulary: poaching, culling, habitat loss, endangered species, reintroduction programme, wildlife protection law.

question: Tusu is a harvest festival celebrated in Jharkhand during the winter in the last day of ______ month.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Poush.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tusu Parab (Makar Parab) is a famous harvest festival of Jharkhand, celebrated on the last day of the month of Poush (Pausha), which falls around mid-January.

◦ It coincides with Makar Sankranti and marks the end of the harvest season.

◦ It is essentially a festival of unmarried girls, who make and decorate a colourful wooden or bamboo frame called the "Tusu" or Chaudal, sing Tusu songs, and finally immerse it in a river or pond.

◦ It is also celebrated in the neighbouring regions of West Bengal (Purulia, Bankura) and Odisha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other festivals of Jharkhand: Sarhul (worship of the sal tree, spring), Karma, Sohrai (cattle festival), Bandna and Jani Shikar.

• The capital of Jharkhand is Ranchi; the state was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000, the birth anniversary of Birsa Munda.

• Sohrai and Khovar painting of Jharkhand has received a GI tag.

NOTE

• Months of the Hindu calendar in order: Chaitra, Vaishakha, Jyeshtha, Ashadha, Shravana, Bhadrapada, Ashvina, Kartika, Margashirsha, Pausha, Magha, Phalguna.

• Chaitra is the first month of the Indian national calendar (Saka era), which was adopted on 22 March 1957.

question: What is the meaning of reverse repo rate?
option_1: Rate at which RBI borrows money from foreign banks
option_2: Rate at which RBI borrows money from commercial banks
option_3: Rate at which commercial banks borrows money from RBI
option_4: Rate at which commercial banks borrows money from foreign banks
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rate at which RBI borrows money from commercial banks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Reverse Repo Rate is the rate at which the Reserve Bank of India borrows money from commercial banks for a short period, against government securities.

◦ It is a tool to absorb excess liquidity from the banking system.

◦ When the reverse repo rate is raised, banks find it attractive to park funds with the RBI, so money supply in the market falls.

• The Repo Rate is the opposite — the rate at which commercial banks borrow money from the RBI against securities; "repo" stands for repurchase agreement.

◦ The reverse repo rate is always lower than the repo rate.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other quantitative instruments of monetary policy:

◦ CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) – the share of deposits banks must keep as cash with the RBI; no interest is paid on it.

◦ SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio) – the share of deposits banks must maintain in the form of cash, gold or approved securities with themselves.

◦ Bank Rate, Open Market Operations (OMO) and the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF).

• Monetary policy is decided by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), a six-member body headed by the RBI Governor, set up in 2016; it targets CPI inflation of 4% (±2%).

NOTE

• Raising the repo rate makes borrowing costlier and is used to control inflation (contractionary policy); lowering it boosts growth (expansionary policy).

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 and nationalised on 1 January 1949; its headquarters is in Mumbai.

question: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth Seekers' Society) in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1873.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jyotiba Phule (Jyotirao Govindrao Phule) founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth Seekers' Society) in 1873 at Pune.

◦ Its aim was to liberate the lower castes and Shudras from Brahmanical dominance, and to work for social justice, equality and education.

◦ It promoted marriages without Brahmin priests and simple, inexpensive ceremonies.

• Other contributions of Jyotiba Phule:

◦ With his wife Savitribai Phule, he opened the first school for girls in Pune in 1848; Savitribai is regarded as India's first woman teacher.

◦ He opened a home for widows and a well for untouchables in his own house.

◦ His famous works: "Gulamgiri" (Slavery, 1873), "Shetkaryacha Asud" (The Cultivator's Whipcord) and "Tritiya Ratna".

◦ He was given the title "Mahatma" in 1888.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other reform bodies of the period: Brahmo Samaj (1828), Prarthana Samaj (1867), Arya Samaj (1875), Theosophical Society (1875) and Ramakrishna Mission (1897).

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar regarded Jyotiba Phule as one of his three gurus, along with the Buddha and Kabir.

NOTE

• The Self-Respect Movement was later launched in the Madras Presidency by E. V. Ramasamy "Periyar" in 1925.

• Shahu Maharaj of Kolhapur introduced reservation for backward classes in his state in 1902.

question: The General Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2021 removes the provision which required the Central Government to have atleast ______ ownership in four subsidiaries of General Insurance Company, namely, National Insurance, New India Assurance, Oriental Insurance, United India Insurance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 51%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Amendment Act, 2021 removed the requirement that the Central Government must hold at least 51% of the equity capital in the specified public sector general insurance companies.

◦ The purpose was to allow greater private participation and to facilitate privatisation/disinvestment in the general insurance sector.

◦ The four subsidiaries concerned are National Insurance Company, New India Assurance, Oriental Insurance and United India Insurance.

◦ The parent Act, the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972, had nationalised the general insurance business in India with effect from 1973.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Life insurance was nationalised earlier — the Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) was set up in 1956.

• The insurance sector is regulated by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), established in 1999 and headquartered at Hyderabad.

• The FDI limit in the insurance sector was raised from 49% to 74% in 2021.

NOTE

• Financial regulators to remember: RBI (banking and monetary policy), SEBI (securities market), IRDAI (insurance) and PFRDA (pensions).

• Disinvestment means the sale of government equity in a public sector undertaking; it is handled by the DIPAM under the Ministry of Finance.

question: Which device is used for measuring temperature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thermometer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A thermometer is the instrument used to measure temperature.

◦ A clinical thermometer measures body temperature, usually over the range 35°C to 42°C (94°F to 108°F); normal human body temperature is about 37°C (98.6°F).

◦ Mercury and alcohol are the liquids traditionally used, because they expand uniformly on heating; digital thermometers are now preferred, since mercury is toxic.

◦ Temperature scales: Celsius (°C), Fahrenheit (°F) and Kelvin (K) — the SI unit is the kelvin.

◦ Conversion: °F = (9/5 × °C) + 32; K = °C + 273.15.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Manometer – measures the pressure of gases or liquids.

• Ammeter – measures electric current (in amperes); it is connected in series in a circuit.

• Barometer – measures atmospheric pressure; a sudden fall indicates a storm, and a steady rise indicates fair weather.

NOTE

• Other instruments frequently asked: Voltmeter (potential difference, connected in parallel), Hygrometer (humidity), Anemometer (wind speed), Seismograph (earthquakes), Lactometer (purity of milk), Hydrometer (density of liquids), Odometer (distance travelled) and Speedometer (speed).

• A pyrometer measures very high temperatures without contact.

question: Who among the following Gupta kings founded the Nalanda University?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kumaragupta I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nalanda Mahavihara was founded by the Gupta emperor Kumaragupta I (c. 415–455 CE) in present-day Nalanda district of Bihar, near Rajgir.

◦ It became the most famous Buddhist monastic university of the ancient world, attracting students from China, Korea, Tibet, Japan and South-East Asia.

◦ The Chinese travellers Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) and I-tsing studied there; Hiuen Tsang visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana.

◦ It was destroyed around 1193 CE by Bakhtiyar Khalji, and the Ruins of the Nalanda Mahavihara were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016.

◦ Kumaragupta I also bore the title Mahendraditya and founded the Ashvamedha tradition in his line of coins.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chandragupta I was the first Gupta ruler to adopt the title Maharajadhiraja, and the Gupta Era began in 319–320 CE.

• Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) defeated the Shakas and took the title Shakari; Fa-Hien visited India during his reign.

• Skandagupta repelled the Huna invasions and repaired the Sudarshana Lake in Saurashtra.

NOTE

• Other ancient centres of learning: Takshashila, Vikramshila and Odantapuri (both founded by Dharmapala of the Pala dynasty), Vallabhi (Gujarat) and Somapura (Bangladesh).

• A modern Nalanda University was re-established at Rajgir, Bihar, under the Nalanda University Act, 2010.

question: Which is the first garden – tomb in the Indian subcontinent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Humayun's Tomb.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Humayun's Tomb in Delhi is the first garden-tomb in the Indian subcontinent.

◦ It was built in 1569–70 by Hamida Banu Begum (Bega Begum), the widow of the Mughal emperor Humayun.

◦ The architect was the Persian Mirak Mirza Ghiyas and his son Sayyid Muhammad.

◦ It is laid out in the charbagh (four-quartered garden) style, divided by water channels, and is built of red sandstone with white marble inlay.

◦ It was the first structure to use red sandstone on such a scale and served as the model for later Mughal tombs, including the Taj Mahal.

◦ It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Taj Mahal (Agra, 1631–53) was built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal; it is a later and more refined development of the same garden-tomb idea.

• The Qutb Shahi Tombs at Hyderabad belong to the rulers of the Golconda (Qutb Shahi) dynasty.

• Aurangzeb's tomb is a simple, unadorned grave at Khuldabad, Maharashtra, in keeping with his austere life.

NOTE

• Humayun died in 1556 after falling from the stairs of his library at Sher Mandal, Purana Qila, Delhi.

• Humayun's Tomb is also called the "dormitory of the Mughals", as several members of the dynasty are buried there; Bahadur Shah Zafar was captured here in 1857.

question: Most of the Himalayan rivers are of which type?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Perennial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Most Himalayan rivers are perennial, that is, they carry water throughout the year.

◦ They are fed by two sources — the melting of Himalayan snow and glaciers in summer, and the monsoon rains — so their flow never dries up.

◦ The three major Himalayan river systems are the Indus, the Ganga and the Brahmaputra.

◦ They have long courses, perform intensive erosion in their upper reaches, and form large meanders, ox-bow lakes, floodplains and deltas in the plains.

• Peninsular rivers, by contrast, are mostly seasonal (non-perennial), since they depend only on monsoon rainfall — examples are the Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Mahanadi, Narmada and Tapi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Indus, Sutlej and Brahmaputra are antecedent rivers — they are older than the Himalayas and cut deep gorges across them.

• The Ganga is India's longest river; the Brahmaputra is known as the Tsangpo in Tibet and the Jamuna in Bangladesh.

• The Indus Waters Treaty (1960) between India and Pakistan was brokered by the World Bank.

NOTE

• An exotic river flows through a desert after originating in a wetter region — the Nile and the Colorado are examples.

• The Sundarbans, formed by the Ganga–Brahmaputra, is the largest delta in the world; the Narmada and Tapi form estuaries, not deltas, as they flow through rift valleys.

question: The Charter Act of 1813 extended the East India Company's rule in India to another ______ years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 20.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Charter Act of 1813 renewed the East India Company's charter for another 20 years.

• Its main provisions:

◦ It ended the Company's trade monopoly in India, throwing Indian trade open to all British merchants; however, the Company retained its monopoly of trade with China and in tea.

◦ It asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over the Company's Indian territories for the first time.

◦ It allowed Christian missionaries to come to India and preach.

◦ It provided a sum of one lakh rupees annually for the revival of literature and the promotion of science among Indians — the first step towards state responsibility for education in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India (Lord William Bentinck being the first) and ended the Company's commercial activities altogether, making it a purely administrative body.

• The Charter Act of 1853 introduced open competition for the civil services and separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council.

• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first British Parliamentary step to control the Company.

NOTE

• The Government of India Act, 1858 abolished the Company and transferred power to the British Crown.

• Macaulay's Minute (1835) made English the medium of instruction, and Wood's Despatch (1854) is called the "Magna Carta of English education in India".

question: The third battle of Panipat fought in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1761.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Third Battle of Panipat was fought on 14 January 1761 between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali (Ahmad Shah Durrani) of Afghanistan.

◦ The Maratha forces were led by Sadashivrao Bhau and Vishwasrao, son of Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao.

◦ Abdali was supported by Najib-ud-Daula of Rohilkhand and Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh.

◦ The Marathas suffered a crushing defeat, which shattered their dream of an all-India empire and indirectly cleared the way for British ascendancy.

• The three battles of Panipat:

◦ First Battle of Panipat (1526) – Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, founding the Mughal Empire.

◦ Second Battle of Panipat (1556) – Akbar's forces under Bairam Khan defeated Hemu (Hemchandra Vikramaditya).

◦ Third Battle of Panipat (1761) – Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Panipat is in present-day Haryana, on the historic route to Delhi from the north-west.

• After the defeat, the Maratha confederacy was revived by Peshwa Madhavrao I, but its unity was permanently weakened.

NOTE

• Babur used field artillery and the Tulughma (flanking) tactic at the First Battle of Panipat.

• Other decisive battles: Plassey (1757), Buxar (1764), Talikota (1565) and the Battle of Haldighati (1576).

question: Who is hailed in India as the Mozart of the Madras?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A.R. Rahman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A. R. Rahman (Allah Rakha Rahman) is famously called the "Mozart of Madras", a title given to him for his extraordinary musical genius.

◦ He won two Academy Awards (Oscars) in 2009 for the film "Slumdog Millionaire" — Best Original Score and Best Original Song ("Jai Ho").

◦ He also won two Grammy Awards, a Golden Globe and a BAFTA.

◦ He has received the Padma Shri (2000), the Padma Bhushan (2010) and several National Film Awards.

◦ His debut as a film composer was with the Tamil film "Roja" (1992), directed by Mani Ratnam.

◦ He composed "Maa Tujhe Salaam" from the album Vande Mataram.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• S. P. Balasubrahmanyam was a legendary playback singer who held a Guinness record for recording the most songs by a male singer; he received the Padma Vibhushan (2021, posthumous).

• Udit Narayan and Arijit Singh are well-known Hindi playback singers.

NOTE

• Other nicknames: Lata Mangeshkar – Nightingale of India; Bismillah Khan – Shehnai maestro; Pandit Ravi Shankar – Godfather of World Music; M. S. Subbulakshmi – Nightingale of Carnatic music.

• Bhanu Athaiya was the first Indian to win an Oscar (Costume Design, Gandhi, 1983); Satyajit Ray received an honorary Oscar in 1992.

question: Baji Rao I or Baji Rao Ballal was the son of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Baji Rao I (Baji Rao Ballal) was the son of Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath and served as Peshwa from 1720 to 1740 under Chhatrapati Shahu.

◦ He is regarded as the greatest of the Peshwas and is famous for never having lost a battle.

◦ He greatly expanded Maratha power northwards and is credited with the policy of striking at the "trunk of the withering tree" — that is, at Mughal Delhi itself.

◦ He defeated the Nizam-ul-Mulk at the Battle of Palkhed (1728) and won the Battle of Bhopal (1737).

◦ Under him the Maratha confederacy took shape, with families such as the Gaekwads (Baroda), Holkars (Indore), Scindias (Gwalior) and Bhonsles (Nagpur) rising to prominence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Balaji Vishwanath was the first Peshwa of the Bhat family; he obtained the rights of Chauth and Sardeshmukhi from the Mughal emperor in 1719.

• Balaji Baji Rao (Nana Saheb) was Baji Rao I's son and Peshwa during the Third Battle of Panipat (1761).

• Madhavrao I revived Maratha power after Panipat; Raghunath Rao (Raghoba) was his uncle, whose intrigues led to the First Anglo-Maratha War.

NOTE

• Shivaji (1630–1680) founded the Maratha kingdom and was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674; his council of eight ministers was the Ashta Pradhan, in which the Peshwa was the chief.

• The Maratha Empire ended with the Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817–18).

question: Bagh Caves, which has 9 Buddhist caves, was developed around the 6th Century AD situated on the Bagh river in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bagh Caves are a group of nine rock-cut Buddhist caves situated on the bank of the Bagh (Baghini) river in the Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh.

◦ They were developed around the 5th–6th century CE, in the post-Gupta period.

◦ They are famous for their mural paintings, which are stylistically very close to those of the Ajanta caves — the caves are sometimes called the "sister of Ajanta".

◦ The paintings are executed in the tempera technique on a mud-plaster ground.

◦ Cave 4, known as the Rang Mahal (Palace of Colours), contains the best-preserved paintings.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other rock-cut caves: Ajanta and Ellora (Maharashtra, both UNESCO sites), Elephanta (Maharashtra), Karle and Bhaja (Maharashtra), Udayagiri-Khandagiri (Odisha, Jain) and Barabara Caves (Bihar, the oldest, of the Mauryan period, given to the Ajivikas by Ashoka).

• Ajanta caves are entirely Buddhist; Ellora has Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves, including the monolithic Kailasa temple built by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.

NOTE

• Madhya Pradesh also has the Bhimbetka rock shelters (prehistoric paintings), the Sanchi Stupa, the Khajuraho temples and the Buddhist monuments at Sanchi — all UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

• The capital of Madhya Pradesh is Bhopal, and the state is called the "Heart of India".

question: Rajagriha was the first capital of which Mahajanapada?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Magadha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rajagriha (Rajgir, in present-day Bihar) was the first capital of the Magadha Mahajanapada.

◦ It was also called Girivraja, as it was surrounded by five hills, which gave it great natural defence.

◦ The capital was later shifted to Pataliputra by Udayin, son of Ajatashatru.

• Magadha rose to become the most powerful of the 16 Mahajanapadas because of:

◦ Rich iron ore deposits near Rajgir, fertile alluvial soil and its position on the Ganga for trade.

◦ Able rulers such as Bimbisara, Ajatashatru and Mahapadma Nanda.

◦ The first Buddhist Council was held at Rajagriha soon after the Buddha's death, under the patronage of Ajatashatru.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Capitals of other Mahajanapadas: Kuru – Indraprastha/Hastinapur; Kosala – Shravasti (and Ayodhya); Avanti – Ujjain and Mahishmati; Vatsa – Kaushambi; Vajji (Vrijji) – Vaishali; Anga – Champa; Panchala – Ahichchhatra and Kampilya.

• The dynasties of Magadha in order: Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya.

NOTE

• The 16 Mahajanapadas are described in the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya.

• Vaishali (Vajji) is regarded as one of the earliest republics (gana-sanghas) in the world.

question: If we sum the gross value added of all the firms of the economy in a year, we get a measure of the value of aggregate amount of goods and services produced by the economy in a year. Such an estimate is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gross domestic product.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sum of the gross value added (GVA) of all the firms in an economy in a year gives the Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

◦ GDP is the money value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country in one year.

◦ Gross Value Added = Value of output – Value of intermediate consumption; only the value added is counted to avoid double counting.

◦ GDP at market price = GVA at basic prices + Product taxes – Product subsidies.

• The three methods of measuring national income are the product (value added) method, the income method and the expenditure method; all three give the same result.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Key relationships:

◦ GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad.

◦ NNP = GNP – Depreciation.

◦ NNP at factor cost = National Income.

◦ Net value added = Gross value added – Depreciation.

• Real GDP is measured at constant (base year) prices, while nominal GDP is at current prices; GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP ÷ Real GDP) × 100.

NOTE

• National income estimates in India are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

• The National Income Committee (1949) was chaired by P. C. Mahalanobis, who is called the Father of Indian Statistics; National Statistics Day is observed on 29 June, his birth anniversary.

question: The oceanic crust mainly consists of ______ and ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is silica, magnesium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The oceanic crust is mainly composed of silica (Si) and magnesium (Ma), and is therefore called "SIMA".

◦ It is made largely of basaltic rock, is denser (about 3.0 g/cm³) and thinner (about 5 km) than the continental crust.

• The continental crust is composed mainly of silica (Si) and alumina (Al), and is called "SIAL".

◦ It is made largely of granitic rock, is lighter (about 2.7 g/cm³) and thicker (about 30 km, up to 70 km under mountains).

◦ Because SIAL is lighter, the continents effectively "float" on the denser SIMA — the principle of isostasy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The three layers of the earth's interior: the Crust, the Mantle and the Core.

◦ The mantle (NIFE-rich upper part called SIMA/mantle) extends to about 2,900 km; the asthenosphere is the source of magma.

◦ The core is composed mainly of nickel (Ni) and iron (Fe), hence called NIFE; the outer core is liquid and the inner core solid.

• Discontinuities: Mohorovicic (Moho) between crust and mantle; Gutenberg between mantle and core; Lehmann between outer and inner core; Conrad within the crust.

NOTE

• The theory of plate tectonics explains earthquakes, volcanoes and mountain building; the theory of continental drift was proposed by Alfred Wegener (1912).

• Seismic waves — P (primary/longitudinal), S (secondary/transverse) and L (surface) — reveal the earth's internal structure; S-waves cannot pass through liquids, which proved that the outer core is liquid.

question: As per census 2011, which among the following Union Territories of India has least population density per square kilometre?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands had the lowest population density among the Union Territories, at about 46 persons per square kilometre.

◦ Population density = Total population ÷ Total area (in sq km).

• Related Census 2011 density figures:

◦ India's average density – 382 persons per sq km.

◦ Highest density among UTs – Delhi (11,320); Chandigarh (9,258) was next.

◦ Highest density among States – Bihar (1,106), followed by West Bengal and Kerala.

◦ Lowest density among States – Arunachal Pradesh (17), followed by Mizoram.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other Census 2011 highlights: population 121.09 crore, sex ratio 943, literacy rate 74.04%, decadal growth 17.7%.

• Jammu and Kashmir was a State at the time of Census 2011; it became a Union Territory on 31 October 2019 under the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019.

NOTE

• The capital of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is Port Blair; Indira Point on Great Nicobar is the southernmost point of India.

• India presently has 28 States and 8 Union Territories.

question: Which of the following programme was launched in 1999?
option_2: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee scheme
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) was launched on 1 April 1999 by the Ministry of Rural Development.

◦ Its objective was to bring the assisted poor families (swarozgaris) above the poverty line by organising them into Self Help Groups (SHGs) and providing bank credit and government subsidy.

◦ It merged several earlier schemes, including the IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA, SITRA, GKY and the Million Wells Scheme.

◦ In 2011 it was restructured as the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM), later renamed Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – NRLM (DAY-NRLM).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• MGNREGA was enacted in 2005 (implemented from 2 February 2006) and guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.

• Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana was launched in 2000-01 for basic rural needs such as health, education, drinking water, housing and rural roads.

• The Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) was launched in 1995 through the KVIC.

NOTE

• Other rural schemes: PMGSY (2000) for rural roads, Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Gramin (2016) for rural housing, and DDU-GKY for rural skill development.

• The word "Swarnajayanti" refers to the golden jubilee of India's independence (1997).

question: Pandit Birju Maharaj was honoured with Padma Vibhushan award for which form of classical dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Birju Maharaj (1938–2022) was the legendary exponent of the classical dance form Kathak, and was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 1986.

◦ He belonged to the Lucknow (Kalka-Bindadin) gharana of Kathak and was the son of Achhan Maharaj.

◦ He also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and a National Film Award for choreography.

◦ He choreographed dance sequences for films such as Devdas, Bajirao Mastani and Umrao Jaan.

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh):

◦ The name comes from "Katha" (story) — the kathakars were storytellers who narrated epics through dance.

◦ It is marked by intricate footwork (tatkar), rapid spins (chakkars) and expressive abhinaya.

◦ Its three main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras (with Raigarh as a fourth).

◦ It is the only classical dance strongly influenced by both Hindu and Mughal court traditions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other Kathak exponents: Sitara Devi, Shovana Narayan, Gopi Krishna and Damayanti Joshi.

• Jhumar is a folk dance of Punjab and Haryana, not a classical form.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri and Sattriya.

• Order of civilian awards: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri; they were instituted in 1954.

question: Which of the following book is the autobiography of Milkha Singh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Race of My Life.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Race of My Life: An Autobiography" was written by the legendary Indian sprinter Milkha Singh together with his daughter Sonia Sanwalka, and published in 2013.

◦ The Bollywood film "Bhaag Milkha Bhaag" (2013) was based on this book.

• About Milkha Singh, known as "The Flying Sikh":

◦ He famously finished fourth in the 400 m final at the Rome Olympics 1960, missing a bronze by a whisker.

◦ He won gold at the Asian Games (1958 and 1962) and at the Commonwealth Games 1958 (Cardiff) — India's first individual athletics gold at the Commonwealth Games.

◦ He was awarded the Padma Shri in 1959.

◦ The title "Flying Sikh" was given to him by the Pakistani General Ayub Khan after he won a race in Lahore.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Touch Play" is a book by the cricketer Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi; "Two Lives" was written by Vikram Seth; "Romancing with Life" is the autobiography of Dev Anand.

• Other sports autobiographies: "Playing It My Way" – Sachin Tendulkar; "The Test of My Life" – Yuvraj Singh; "Unbreakable" – Mary Kom; "Ace Against Odds" – Sania Mirza; "Straight from the Heart" – Kapil Dev.

NOTE

• P. T. Usha, called the "Payyoli Express" and the "Golden Girl", also finished fourth (in the 400 m hurdles) at the Los Angeles Olympics 1984.

• Neeraj Chopra won India's first Olympic gold in athletics at Tokyo 2020.

question: Kathakali took shape in Southern India in the seventeenth century under the patronage of the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prince of Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kathakali took its present shape in southern India in the seventeenth century under royal patronage, and the option accepted in the official answer key is the Prince of Karnataka.

• About Kathakali:

◦ It is the classical dance-drama of Kerala; the name literally means "story-play" (katha = story, kali = play).

◦ Its themes are drawn from the Ramayana, the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

◦ It is traditionally performed by male dancers, who convey the story through mudras (hand gestures) and facial expressions, with no spoken dialogue.

◦ It is famous for its elaborate make-up (chutti), towering headgear and colour codes — Pacha (green, for noble characters), Kathi (for villainous but heroic ones), Thadi (bearded), Kari (black, for demons) and Minukku (for women and sages).

◦ Instruments used: chenda, maddalam, chengila and elathalam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The form is generally traced to Ramanattam, created in the 17th century by the Raja of Kottarakkara (Kottarakkara Thampuran) in Kerala, which developed into Kathakali.

• Famous exponents: Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair, Guru Kunchu Kurup and Kalamandalam Gopi.

• The poet Vallathol Narayana Menon founded the Kerala Kalamandalam (1930), which revived Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

NOTE

• Kerala's other classical form is Mohiniyattam, a graceful solo dance performed by women.

• Koodiyattam, the Sanskrit theatre of Kerala, was recognised by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2001.

question: Under which type of unemployment a person contributes less than their capability?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Disguised unemployment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Disguised unemployment exists when more people are engaged in a job than are actually required, so each person contributes less than his or her full capability.

◦ The marginal productivity of such workers is zero — if they are withdrawn, total output does not fall.

◦ It is also called hidden unemployment, because the persons appear to be employed but are effectively surplus.

◦ It is very widespread in Indian agriculture, where an entire family may work on a small plot that two people could manage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Frictional unemployment – short-term unemployment while a person is changing jobs or searching for a first job.

• Cyclical unemployment – caused by the downswing of the business cycle, when aggregate demand falls (as in a depression).

• Seasonal unemployment – occurs during particular seasons, common in agriculture, tourism and the sugar industry.

• Structural unemployment – caused by a mismatch between workers' skills and available jobs, due to technological or structural change.

• Educated unemployment – educated youth unable to find suitable jobs, a major problem in urban India.

NOTE

• Employment and unemployment data in India come from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) of the NSO, conducted since 2017-18.

• Disguised unemployment is a feature of underdeveloped economies with surplus labour in the primary sector.

question: The First Field Handball World Championships were played in Germany in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1938.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first Field Handball World Championship was played in Germany in 1938, and the host nation Germany won the title.

◦ In the same year the first indoor handball world championship was also held in Germany.

◦ Field handball was played outdoors with 11 players per side, while modern indoor handball is played with 7 players per side.

• About handball:

◦ It is governed by the International Handball Federation (IHF), founded in 1946 and headquartered at Basel, Switzerland.

◦ Field handball featured at the Berlin Olympics 1936; indoor handball became a permanent Olympic sport at Munich 1972 (women's from Montreal 1976).

◦ A modern indoor match lasts two halves of 30 minutes each.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Handball Federation of India governs the sport in the country.

• The International Amateur Handball Federation (the predecessor of the IHF) was formed in 1928, the year of the Amsterdam Olympics.

NOTE

• Number of players in some games: Cricket 11, Football 11, Hockey 11, Handball 7 (indoor), Basketball 5, Volleyball 6, Kabaddi 7, Kho-Kho 9 (now 7 in some formats), Water Polo 7, Polo 4.

• Sports headquarters worth remembering: FIFA – Zurich; IOC – Lausanne; ICC – Dubai; FIH – Lausanne; BWF – Kuala Lumpur.

question: The cells having nuclear material without nuclear membrane are termed as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prokaryotic cells.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Prokaryotic cells are those in which the nuclear material (DNA) is not enclosed by a nuclear membrane; the undefined nuclear region is called the nucleoid. (प्रोकैरियोटिक कोशिका)

◦ The word comes from Greek pro (before) + karyon (nucleus).

◦ They are small (1–10 µm) and lack membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, plastids, the endoplasmic reticulum and the Golgi apparatus.

◦ Their ribosomes are of the 70S type, and they usually have a single circular DNA molecule plus plasmids.

◦ Examples: bacteria, blue-green algae (cyanobacteria), mycoplasma and archaebacteria.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Eukaryotic cells have a well-defined nucleus bounded by a nuclear membrane and possess membrane-bound organelles; their ribosomes are of the 80S type. Examples: all plants, animals, fungi and protozoa — including cheek cells and onion cells, which are simply examples of eukaryotic cells.

• The cell was discovered by Robert Hooke in 1665 in a slice of cork; Leeuwenhoek first saw living cells; Robert Brown discovered the nucleus (1831).

• The Cell Theory was proposed by Schleiden and Schwann (1838-39) and extended by Rudolf Virchow (1855), who stated Omnis cellula e cellula — all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

NOTE

• The mitochondrion is the "powerhouse of the cell", and the lysosome the "suicidal bag"; the ribosome is the site of protein synthesis.

• Plant cells differ from animal cells in having a cell wall (cellulose), plastids and a large central vacuole.

question: Which country is the biggest producer of rice?
solution_text:
The correct answer is China.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• China is the largest producer of rice in the world, followed by India in second place.

◦ India, however, is the largest exporter of rice in the world.

◦ Rice is the staple food of a majority of Indians, especially in the eastern and southern regions.

• Conditions required for rice cultivation:

◦ High temperature (above 25°C), high humidity and annual rainfall above 100 cm; in areas of lower rainfall it is grown with irrigation.

◦ It is a kharif crop, sown with the onset of the monsoon and harvested in September–October.

◦ In West Bengal, three crops of rice are grown in a year — Aus, Aman and Boro.

◦ West Bengal is India's leading rice-producing state, followed by Uttar Pradesh and Punjab.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India is the largest producer of pulses, jute, milk and spices, and the second largest producer of rice, wheat, sugarcane, groundnut, fruits and vegetables.

• The Green Revolution of the 1960s, led by Dr. M. S. Swaminathan (the "Father of the Green Revolution in India") and Norman Borlaug, greatly increased wheat and rice output.

NOTE

• The International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) is at Los Baños, Philippines; India's National Rice Research Institute is at Cuttack, Odisha.

• Golden rice is a genetically modified variety enriched with beta-carotene (Vitamin A).
